articleTitle: Performance limit of two-pump brillouin fiber sensors obtained by Manakov Modulation Instability
abstract: The Manakov modulation instability is shown to determine the performance limit of long-distance Brillouin fiber sensors utilizing orthogonally-polarized pumps. Numerical simulations of the Manakov equation are supported by the experimental measurement of a 25-km Brillouin fiber sensor to verify the model. The study reveals that the use of orthogonallypolarized pulses decreases the pump depletion due to modulation instability leading to an enhancement of the sensing distance.

articleTitle: Data transmission through polarization domain walls in standard telecom optical fibers
abstract: We report the generation and propagation of polarization domain walls in a standard Telecom optical fiber in the normal dispersion regime. These vectorial structures are then implemented in order to transmit optical data at 1550 nm at a 10 GBits/s and 40 GBits/s bit-rate.

articleTitle: Temporal localized states in semiconductors: from spatially extended to delayed systems
abstract: The formation of optical localized states in semiconductor systems has been to date very much focussed on transverse dynamics. In this contribution, we build on some recent publications devoted to dissipative solitons in semiconductors in time domain to discuss the analogy between spatially extended and delayed dynamical systems. In particular, we study front dynamics and homoclinic connections in relation to localized states in delayed systems.

articleTitle: Second harmonic generation in an optically poled fiber
abstract: The second harmonic signal at the output of an optically poled fiber was studied as a function of the input fundamental frequency power and polarization state. For an injected average power of 3 mW at 1064 nm, the measured output power at 532 nm was 10 μW. The second harmonic intensity profile was a bright green ring even if the pump was injected in the fundamental HE11 mode: we believe that the second harmonic was carried by a combination of the EH11 and HE31 modes.

articleTitle: Soliton Stability in Multimode Fibers
abstract: We numerically investigate the stability of solitons in a multimode fiber in the presence of intermodal nonlinear coupling by solving the coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations. While individual fundamental and higher order solitons propagating in any mode are stable, simultaneous propagation of solitons in different modes leads to interesting phenomena on account of intermodal nonlinear coupling. Soliton trapping is also observed under certain conditions such that two solitons in different modes travel at the same speed despite considerable intermodal differential group delay between them. Finally the effect on launching the solitons at different wavelengths is investigated.

articleTitle: Photonic devices with two dimensional materials
abstract: The unique properties of two dimensional materials have been attracting the ever increasing interest of the scientific community since the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics, which was awarded to Novoselov and Geim for their groundbreaking studies on graphene. Scientists have already envisaged a plethora of innovative applications in electronics and photonics which exploit the unique characteristics of this new material platform. Here we will first review the state-of-the-art of modeling of photonic devices based on the co-integration of conventional dielectric waveguides and graphene. Then, we will discuss peculiar temporal and spatial features of one dimensional graphene based edge plasmon polaritons.

articleTitle: Anderson localization of light in synthetic photonic lattices
abstract: We make an comprehensive experimental and theoretical study of an effect of localization of light in photonic lattices realized in time domain with random optical potential. We show that localization occurs in whole range of disorder strength in full agreement with Anderson localization in 1D model. The disorder influence on modes structure is also discussed.

articleTitle: Complex light-matter interactions in photonic crystal fibres
abstract: Twisted photonic crystal fibre (PCF) supports novel helical Bloch modes that uniquely display OAM (orbital angular momentum) birefringence, acoustic resonances trapped in micron-scale glass cores can be used to stably mode-lock soliton fibre lasers at gigahertz rates and gas-filled hollow core PCF is enabling a new generation of bright tunable deep and vacuum ultraviolet light sources.

Author Keywords: photonic crystal fibres; nonlinear optics;optomechanics; orbital angular momentum; high harmonic modelocking

articleTitle: Multicolor filaments and vortex states
abstract: Light filaments results from a nonlinear interaction of light and the medium it propagates. The wellknown Townes soliton profile describes a monochromatic self-guided mode. Here we present work on two fronts: existence and properties of vortex modes and co-existence of two-color filaments.

articleTitle: Longitudinal component of optics field dynamics in self-action of nonparaxial few cycle waves in nonlinear medium
abstract: Modication of the system of equations describes the diffractive spectral dynamics of the field in dispersive nonlinear medium is considered. The result of numerical simulation for the propagation of longitudinal component of TM-polarized wave in a crystal of lithium niobate is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A coherent master equation for active mode locking in lasers
abstract: We present the derivation of a new master equation for active mode locking in lasers that fully takes into account the coherent effects of the light matter interaction through a peculiar adiabatic elimination technique. The coherent effects included in our model could be relevant to describe properly mode-locked semiconductor lasers where the standard Haus’ Master Equation predictions show some discrepancy with respect to the experimental results and can be included in the modelling of other mode locking techniques too.

Author Keywords: mode locking; semiconductor lasers; Maxwell-Bloch equations; coherent effects in mode locking

articleTitle: Photonic crystal lasers and loss compensation in metamaterials
abstract: Incorporation of gain in photonic crystals and metamaterials can be utilized for different purposes. In particular, here we examine how the lasing threshold of a two dimensional photonic crystal (2D PC) containing a four-level gain medium is modified, as a result of the interplay between the group velocity and the modal reflectivity at the interface between the cavity and the exterior. The idea is demonstrated via selfconsistent calculations based on a finite-difference time-domain method. The simulations are in good agreement with theoretical predictions. Using a four-level gain system, we also study light amplification of arrays of metallic split-ring resonators with a gain layer underneath. We find that, while the differential transmittance δT/T is positive for the gain substrate alone, δT/T can be negative for split-ring resonators on the top of the gain substrate, which is not expected. These simulations, which demonstrate reduction of the resonator damping, agree with pump-probe experiments and can help to design new experiments to compensate for the losses of metamaterials.

Author Keywords: Photonic crystals; Laser resonators; Lasers;Metamaterials; Computational electromagnetic methods

articleTitle: Self-increased acceptance bandwidth of second harmonic generation for high-energy light sources
abstract: We report a series of experimental results showing that the acceptance bandwidth of second harmonic generation in quadratic crystals may substantially broaden when using pumps at high intensities. We highlight the co-existence of second harmonic generation and strong unconventional spatial beam reshaping. Our experimental results are in good agreement with our numerical simulations.

Author Keywords: nonlinear optics; parametric processes; harmonicgeneration and mixing; nonlinear optical materials

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal pulse propagation in multimode fibers
abstract: Nonlinear wave propagation in multimode optical fibers will be introduced. Recent theoretical and experimental progress on intense pulse propagation in multimode fibers will be reviewed, with an emphasis on spatiotemporal aspects of the wave propagation.

articleTitle: Generation and characterization of ultrashort airy pulses
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of ultrashort Airy pulses with tailored duration and acceleration properties. Their full temporal evolution is mapped in a flexible and simple one beam experiment, which features a tunable dispersion element and an intrinsic time reference. Using this setup we can experimentally verify the nondispersiveness and self-acceleration of the Airy pulses.

articleTitle: Quantum photonic circuits for optical signal processing
abstract: In this talk, the physics of microring resonators is discussed in the classical and quantum regimes, in the context of the exploitation of chi-3 effects in these cavities as done by our group. Through the implementation of a novel microring pumping scheme and a quantum reinterpretation of the frequency comb, we present an integrated platform for the generation of quantum optical states spread over multiple optical modes. The scheme allows for highly stable and potentially fullyintegrable quantum light sources. Following the demonstration of a multiplexed heralded photon source, the scheme also enabled the first demonstration of a new nonlinear process on the integrated platform (type II spontaneous four-wave mixing) allowing the first direct generation of polarization-diverse photon pairs, where the first time two ring modes can be pumped in a stable configuration.

Author Keywords: Quantum optics; Integrated optics devices;Nonlinear optics

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal spectra dynamics of few-cycle optical waves at noncollinear interaction in nonlinear medium
abstract: Numerical modelling of the noncollinear interaction of few-cycle waves in a medium with inertialess cubic nonlinearity was conducted. Significant change the efficiency of the tripled frequency radiation generation due the interaction was shown.

articleTitle: Light propagation management in complex photonic lattices
abstract: Here, an overview of the main results for light propagation and control over it in composite complex photonic lattices based on photorefractive materials is presented.

articleTitle: Stochastic anti-resonance in a fibre raman amplifier
abstract: Stochastic anti-resonance, that is resonant enhancement of randomness caused by polarization mode beatings, is analyzed both numerically and analytically on an example of fibre Raman amplifier with randomly varying birefringence. As a result of such anti-resonance, the polarization mode dispersion growth causes an escape of the signal state of polarization from a metastable state corresponding to the pulling of the signal to the pump state of polarization.This phenomenon reveals itself in abrupt growth of gain fluctuations as well as in dropping of Hurst parameter and Kramers length characterizing long memory in a system and noise induced escape from the polarization pulling state. The results based on analytical multiscale averaging technique agree perfectly with the numerical data obtained by direct numerical simulations of underlying stochastic differential equations. This challenging outcome would allow replacing the cumbersome numerical simulations for real-world extra-long high-speed communication systems.

Author Keywords: stochastic anti-resonance; fibre Raman amplifier;telecommunication systems; multi-scaling; stochastic differentialequations

articleTitle: Complex temporal dynamics in optical cavities
abstract: We overview recent advances in the modeling and understanding of complex spatiotemporal dynamics associated with the generation of optical frequency combs in microresonators.

articleTitle: Control and manipulation of modulation instability
abstract: We demonstrate a new mechanism for the suppression of modulation instability in a wide class of spatially distributed nonlinear systems. This is done by a periodic spatio-temporal modulation of the background potential. The phenomenon is general in nature as it is shown on a universal model of Complex Ginzburg-Landau equation, and can be extended to various different systems. The results are demonstrated using a modified Floquet linear stability analysis and through direct numerical integration.

articleTitle: Hybrid silica nanowires with a highly nonlinear glass think coating
abstract: We report on the fabrication of hybrid photonic nanowires consisting of silica tapered fibers covered with a thin layer (< 100 nm) of a sol-gel derived highly nonlinear glass (HNG). These hybrid nanowires exhibit finely tunable waveguide properties: The deposition of a single layer of high index glass around the silica taper in sound to be sufficient for obtaining zero-dispersion operating wavelenghts at any point throughout the visible to mid-infrared range, while both positions and values of id

articleTitle: Existence and dynamics of pairs of temporal cavity solitons weakly-bound through kelly sidebands in a passive optical fiber resonator
abstract: We report experimental observations of weaklybound states of temporal cavity solitons, with separations of 10 soliton widths and beyond, in a 100-m single mode fiber cavity. Bound state dynamics has been studied using the real time dispersive Fourier transform technique for roundtrip-byroundtrip measurements. Temporal oscillations in the cavity soliton background, associated with the presence of Kelly sidebands, have been identified as the binding mechanism.

Author Keywords: cavity soliton; bound states; Kelly sidebands;dispersive Fourier transform

articleTitle: Temporal localized states in semiconductors (II): from mode-locking to localized pulses
abstract: In this presentation we will review the results recently obtained on Time-Localized Structures (TLS) in VCSELs coupled to an external cavity. We show that, when the cavity roundtrip is much larger than the medium timescales, this system exhibits a temporal aspect-ratio large enough to host TLS. Two configurations will be considered. In the first one the system is submitted to cross-polarization reinjection which leads to the formation of vectorial TLS. In the second one the external mirror is a Saturable Absorber Mirror, a scheme commonly used for achieving active mode-locking. Here we will show how modelocking pulses become TLS and how they can be manipulated by a current modulation.

articleTitle: Revealing spatio-temporal regimes of generation in raman fiber lasers
abstract: We present here experimental observation of different spatio-temporal generation regimes in quasi-CW Raman fiber laser in the most simple experimental configuration. The generation regimes depend on pump power and range from partial mode-locking to turbulent, and a generation of short-lived pulses. While in temporal domain transitions could be described in quantitative way, in spatio-temporal domain they represent qualitative change in observed dynamics.

articleTitle: Mode-locked all-fiber laser with cascaded generation of Raman dissipative solitons
abstract: We demonstrate cascaded generation of first- and second-order Raman dissipative solitons in an all-fiber laser cavity. Optimization and coherent combining of dissipative soliton and second-order Raman dissipative soliton is performed.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal extreme events in a laser with saturable absorber
abstract: Extreme events in optics have been recently attracting a great attention due to the well-known analogy between optics and hydrodynamics, where rogue wave formation and prediction is a priority field of investigations. In this contribution, we show numerical results about extreme events occurring in the transverse section of the field emitted by a broad-area semiconductor laser with saturable absorber. We believe that our system, being intrinsically two-dimensional, may give some precious insights on the focusing mechanisms giving rise to rogue wave formation in oceans, mechanisms that could be absent in one-dimensional systems.

articleTitle: Effects of conjugate fields on the nonlinear propagation of light
abstract: We have studied the influence of the nonlinear interaction between the electromagnetic field and its conjugate ('negative frequency field') through the inclusion of new terms in the nonlinear polarisation. We have found that this new terms modify the usual nonlinear Self-phase modulation as well as giving rise to completely new phase-matched radiations emitted by light propagating in microresonators and fiber loops.
